text.p: Cosmetics giant L'Oreal reported on Thursday that net attributable profit before capital gains and losses rose 10.3 percent in 1996 to 3.73 billion francs ($655 million), helped by a profit surge at its drugs subsidiary Synthelabo.

Synthelabo's operating profit jumped 25 percent to 1.52 billion francs last year, compared with a 16 percent rise in operating profit to 5.85 billion for the cosmetics business, whose brands range from Lancome to Maybelline.
L'Oreal said in a statement consolidated 1996 sales rose 13 percent to 60.35 billion francs, boosted by the acquisitions of U.S.-based Maybelline, Jade of Germany and Interbeauty in Israel.

The French company said that although overall operating profit rose 17.5 percent to 7.36 billion francs, higher financial expenses related to the acquisitions resulted in a smaller rise in net attributable profit.
It said the 1996 results were provisional and still pending clearance by the board and auditors.

L'Oreal said corporate tax rose 14.8 percent last year and that the portion paid to minority interests also increased, reflecting growth in Synthelabo's earnings, due to a strong performance by some of its drugs.
"Consequently net profit before capital gains and losses, after minority interests...reached 3.73 billion francs, up 10.3 percent," it said.
